name: Songen Gu

papers.title: τ0-WM: A Unified Video-Action World Model for Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Robotic manipulation requires models that generate executable actions while anticipating and evaluating their future consequences before physical execution. We present $\tau_0$-World Model ($\tau_0$-WM), a unified video-action world model that integrates policy learning, video prediction, and action evaluation within a single future-predictive framework. Built on a shared video diffusion backbone, $\tau_0$-WM provides two complementary interfaces. First, a video action model jointly predicts future visual latents and continuous action chunks from multi-view observations, language instructions, and robot state. Second, an action-conditioned video simulator rolls out candidate action chunks into multi-view futures with dense task-progress scores. The model is trained on approximately $27{,}300$ hours of real-robot teleoperation, UMI-style interaction, egocentric human videos, and rollout or failure trajectories using modality-specific supervision masks. At inference time, $\tau_0$-WM uses test-time computation to sample action candidates, rank them with re-denoising consistency, and invoke simulator-based rectification for low-quality candidates. On challenging long-horizon and fine-grained robotic manipulation tasks, this procedure improves average performance over relevant baselines.

papers.title: World In Your Hands: A Large-scale Dataset for Learning Ego-centric Robotic Manipulation In-the-Wild
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce World In Your Hands (WIYH), a large-scale ego-centric dataset comprising over 1,000 hours of ego manipulation data collected in the wild with millimeter-scale motion accuracy. WIYH is built around three components: (1) Oracle Suite, a wearable data-collection kit with an auto-labeling and validation pipeline for accurate motion capture; (2) the WIYH Dataset, which contains diverse multimodal manipulation demonstrations across hundreds of skills and real-world scenarios; and (3) comprehensive annotations, including calibrated visual observations, 3D hand and wrist trajectories, depth, masks, task and sub-task language, and vision-language supervision. We evaluate WIYH through a preliminary real-robot co-training study and a main pre-training study in RoboCasa and on real robots. The results show that ego-centric data improves manipulation policies when robot data are accurate but narrow and that verified WIYH annotations provide substantially stronger pretraining signals than unverified ego data, even when the latter contains more samples. WIYH provides a foundation for studying scalable ego-centric data collection and annotation-quality-aware robot policy learning. All data and documents will be open-sourced.
